audit_notes: Model: steady 1D series conduction interior -> wall -> sealed air chamber -> shell; the normalized gradient dT_dx spans the full resistance R_tot = 1/U_wall + R_gap, so q = dT_dx/R_tot. Outer boundary is a linearised sol-air balance on the shell. Closed form: q = [alpha*I + h*(T_a - T_in) - eps*R_net]/(1 + h*R_tot). Adjustments: the concept is a facade cladding, but the proposal used horizontal-roof numbers. For a west/east facade in a hot climate the daily-mean irradiance is ~150-200 W/m2 (I set 180) and the net longwave loss of a vertical surface, which sees half sky and half warm ground/buildings, is ~30-45 W/m2 (I set 40). R_gap = 0.5 m2K/W is consistent with ISO 6946 for a 40 mm unventilated vertical cavity with one low-e face (h_a ~1.25, h_r ~0.3 W/m2K -> ~0.6); I keep 0.5 to allow for dust and condensation on the low-e face over 20 years. Aged glazed ceramic SR 0.75 is plausible (glazes are smooth and rain-washed; white glazes start ~0.80). Dimensionless: Biot-type ratio h*R_tot = 37.5 (design) vs 30 (baseline); Rayleigh number of the 40 mm cavity at dT ~ 3 K: Ra ~ g*beta*dT*d^3/(nu*alpha) = 9.81*(1/308)*3*6.4e-5/(1.6e-5*2.2e-5) ~ 1.7e4, i.e. weak cellular convection, consistent with ISO values. Simulation coefficient: effective assembly conductance U_eff = 1/(R_tot + 1/h) = 0.39 W/m2K. Hand solution: design q = (45 + 150 - 36)/(1 + 37.5) = 4.13 W/m2; baseline (aged white paint SR 0.67 directly on the wall, R_gap = 0): (59.4 + 150 - 36)/(1 + 30) = 5.59 W/m2; gain ~26 %. Important: most of this gain comes from the added cavity resistance, which a thicker conventional insulation layer would also give; the reflective-shell part alone is ~5 %. Structural: ceramic shells ~10 mm thick on stainless anchors carry wind suction of ~1-2 kPa easily; fired glaze is UV-stable for decades; risks are anchor corrosion, breakage by hail/impact and cracked seals letting dust into the chamber. Baseline: aged white acrylic facade coating directly on the same wall (map baseline).
